standard_prerequisites.name: Basic properties of henselization, and Noetherianity of the henselization and strict henselization
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Lemmas \ref{lemma-dumb-properties-henselization} and \ref{lemma-henselization-noetherian}, cited at proof lines 11295-11296
standard_prerequisites.use: Supply the properties used without mention throughout, in particular finiteness of the number of minimal primes.

standard_prerequisites.name: The henselization of a quotient is the quotient of the henselization
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, Lemma \ref{algebra-lemma-quotient-henselization} and Algebra, Lemma \ref{algebra-lemma-quotient-strict-henselization}, cited at proof lines 11298-11300
standard_prerequisites.use: Allow the reduction to the case where the ring is a domain and the prime is zero.

standard_prerequisites.name: A domain has reduced henselization
standard_prerequisites.use: Makes the base change reduced, so that its primes are minimal and maximal at once.

standard_prerequisites.name: A reduced Noetherian ring of dimension zero is a product of fields
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, Proposition \ref{algebra-proposition-dimension-zero-ring} and Algebra, Lemma \ref{algebra-lemma-minimal-prime-reduced-ring}, cited at proof lines 11314-11317
standard_prerequisites.use: Identify the base change with the product of the residue fields of the primes over the prime.

standard_prerequisites.name: Residue field extensions of etale ring maps are finite separable
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, Lemma \ref{algebra-lemma-etale-at-prime}, cited at proof lines 11321-11324
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that the residue field extensions obtained from the colimit presentation are separable algebraic.

core_obligations: Record that the henselization of the quotient by the prime is the quotient of the henselization, and reduce to a Noetherian local domain with prime zero (proof lines 11297-11303).
List the finitely many minimal primes of the henselization and identify them with the primes over zero using flatness and going down (proof lines 11304-11306).
Deduce reducedness of the henselization from the domain hypothesis (proof lines 11307-11308).
Show the base change is reduced with finitely many primes, all minimal and maximal, hence Artinian and a product of fields (proof lines 11309-11317).
Read the separable algebraic statement off the colimit presentation by etale ring maps (proof lines 11318-11326).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to a domain with prime zero (proof lines 11297-11303).
Identify the primes over the prime and reducedness (proof lines 11304-11308).
Show the base change is a product of fields (proof lines 11309-11317).
Get separability from the etale colimit presentation (proof lines 11318-11326).
difficulty_reason: The lemma computes the base change of the henselization and of the strict henselization of a Noetherian local ring along the residue field of a prime: it is a finite product of the residue fields of the primes lying over that prime, and each of those extensions is separable algebraic. The author notes that the result follows from a more general filtered-colimit statement and then gives a direct proof: after replacing the ring by its quotient by the prime, the henselization is Noetherian, so it has finitely many minimal primes, which by flatness and going down are exactly the primes over zero, and reducedness makes the base change a reduced Artinian ring, hence a product of fields. The separability statement is read off from the presentation of the henselization as a colimit of etale ring maps.
